paper_metadata.title: On the potential of quantum walks for modeling financial return distributions

summary: The paper proposes a theoretical discrete-time quantum walk model for financial return distributions and explores parameter regimes (e.g., time steps n up to 220 and decoherence probabilities p up to 0.5) using classical simulations averaged over 1000 runs. It shows that the quantum walk variance scales as n² (ballistic diffusion) compared with classical t scaling and demonstrates tunable skewness (≈ −1.04 to 0) and entropy properties through coin parameters and decoherence.

experiments.description: Theoretical discrete-time quantum walk model for financial return distributions, including unitary walks and decoherence variants, compared against classical GBM, Lévy stable, and power-law baselines; no hardware execution is reported.

algorithm.variant: discrete-time quantum walk with SU(2) coin; Hadamard coin special case; decoherence via broken links or random phase
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial coin states explicitly chosen; Hadamard coin used in several figures; decoherence parameters swept over reported values

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One-dimensional position space of the quantum walk models financial return increments; position j corresponds to return outcomes
problem_formulation.objective_function: Model the temporal evolution of asset prices/return distributions via discrete-time quantum walk dynamics and compare resulting distributions to classical financial return models
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Decoherence introduced by stochastic link disruption or random coin phase to interpolate between quantum and classical behavior

problem_instance.description: Synthetic/theoretical financial return-distribution modeling study; no empirical market dataset used

dataset_specification.description: No real-market dataset; distributions generated analytically/simulated from the quantum walk model

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical comparison of distribution shape, skewness, variance, Shannon entropy, and qualitative comparison to Gaussian, Lévy stable, and power-law models; decoherent cases averaged over 1000 simulations

noise_model.noise_type: algorithmic decoherence (broken-link model and random coin phase)

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute and compare skewness, variance, Shannon entropy, and return distributions; normalize distributions for plotting/comparison

classical_baselines.value: classical random walk reference; exact value not numerically stated except for theta=pi/2 case
reference curve shown in figure; exact numeric values not stated
reached at p = 0.5 for broken-link decoherence and at tilde_p = 1 for random-phase decoherence
reference distribution; exact numeric value not stated
lower tail risk than decoherent quantum walk; no numeric value stated

speedup_claims.factor: efficient implementation on a quantum computing device
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical random walk / classical financial simulation
speedup_claims.conditions: for a one-dimensional quantum walk circuit
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper cites prior work stating that a 1D quantum walk circuit can be implemented efficiently, but does not provide a concrete asymptotic speedup or hardware benchmark.
No gate-based hardware experiment, runtime benchmark, or empirical speedup is reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Discrete-time quantum walk on a line can be implemented efficiently; paper states a one-dimensional quantum walk circuit can be implemented efficiently on a quantum computing device

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not specified; the paper only analyzes abstract discrete-time quantum walks and does not provide resource estimates for a circuit implementation.
limiting_factors: No circuit-level implementation or qubit counts provided
All results generated from theoretical analysis and classical simulations
No complexity comparison demonstrating asymptotic speedup over classical financial models
No hardware execution or NISQ evaluation

notes: No actual quantum hardware experiment is reported; the paper is a theoretical/simulation study of quantum walks for finance.

num_qubits is not explicitly stated because the paper discusses the walk in abstract Hilbert-space terms rather than a concrete circuit implementation; only the general claim that a 1D quantum walk circuit can be implemented efficiently is reported.
circuit_depth is not given as a gate-depth number; the paper reports time steps n for the walk, which are used here as the closest reported circuit-depth analogue for the abstract model.
The authors do not claim computational quantum advantage; they position quantum walks as a flexible modeling framework.
All experiments are theoretical or classical simulations (1000-run averages in figures) with no QPU execution.
